gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a PLA build plate costs per printable side. BIQU's double-sided CryoGrip Pro plate for Bambu printers starts at $19.99 on BIQU's US store today, which works out to about $10.00 per side.
standout_why: I opened the Prusa PLA article (cited), the Prusa flexible steel sheets guidepost (cited), Nozzle Notes' build-plate article and 3D Adapt's smooth/textured/satin guide. None of them gives a price, a cost per side, a lifespan or a print count. Nozzle Notes says outright that it has no prices or lifespan figures. All four only describe surfaces and bed temperatures, so a dollars-per-side number is new.
decides: It doesn't settle the pick yet. It shows the BIQU CryoGrip Pro is a two-surface plate starting at $19.99, about $10 per side, and the Glacier listing rates PLA at 45–55°C, below Prusa's 60°C recommendation. I could not open Bambu Lab's US store or wiki, so there is no matching cost per side for the Bambu Textured PEI or Cool Plate SuperTack. Use it to confirm the BIQU plate's value; don't rank it against the Bambu plates on price until those prices are sourced.

Bambu Lab Textured PEI Plate US price: same Bambu store block, so I couldn't compute its cost per side.
Number of coated sides on the Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack and on the Textured PEI plate: wiki.bambulab.com returned HTTP 402.

Prices for each BIQU variant (Frostbite 257, Frostbite 180 A1 mini, Glacier 257): every storecheck product request and direct fetch of the BIQU product pages returned HTTP 429, so I only have each listing's lowest price.

Energy saved per print from a lower bed temperature: I found no maker figure for the bed heater's wattage or heat-up energy at a given temperature, and BIQU states its energy saving only qualitatively.
Plate lifespan or print count for any candidate: no maker or reviewer figure on any page I opened. Prusa only says coatings wear over time.
